Hi Marissa / Karthik,

Thanks again — Rackline is finalizing the colo topology for the Edge Pod that will host Redwood Private. Before we lock circuits I wanted to run our proposed "orthogonal planes" reference across your team to make sure the control plane footprint and egress constraints match Redwood's expectations. I attached the current diagram (rackline-orthoplane-initial.pdf).

Key asks:
- Confirm control plane HA placement (we currently show 2 control plane nodes in Zone A, standby in Zone B).
- Validate egress model: customer traffic -> tenant NAT -> outbound internet via shared egress. Any constraints on return-path or source IP preservation?
- Do you require an mTLS terminator inside the tenant boundary or will your sidecar handle mutual auth to the control plane?
- Any inventory / firewall ACLs you need from our side for SOC evidence?

Attached files: rackline-orthoplane-initial.pdf (diagram)

If it's easier we can do a short 30-minute run-through Monday — but a quick reply with notes would be great.

Hi Stelios — thanks for sending this over. I reviewed the attached PDF and sketched a short set of ops/acceptance notes (attached: marissa-ops-annotated-v1.pdf). High-level responses inline below to your numbered asks, and a few additional operational asks.

1) Control plane HA placement
- Short answer: 2x active in Zone A with standby in Zone B is fine provided you guarantee cross-zone latency < 10ms for our heartbeat RPCs. If latency could spike we prefer 1 active per zone with synchronous replication disabled and a fast failover mechanism.

2) Egress model / NAT
- We can support a tenant-side NAT model. Important items: preserve source port mapping when possible (some telemetry correlates by 5-tuple) and include a stable egress IP pool per tenant for audit logs.

3) mTLS termination
- Redwood's preferred pattern is the tenant sidecar handling mTLS to the control plane (mutual auth). We will provide cert bundles and an automated rotation endpoint. If Rackline prefers a perimeter terminator, we need an assurance that per-tenant identities are preserved and cert rotation will be supported.

4) ACL / SOC evidence
- Please provide: control-plane ingress CIDR list, egress IPs for your monitoring estate, and timing windows for scheduled maintenance. We will add these items to the SOC evidence pack.

Operational asks (new):
- Can you map the POD-subnet => Rackline VLAN ids on the diagram? We need explicit mapping for cutover runbooks.
- Add a note about your outage policy and expected MTTRs for physical network faults.

Next steps: I've attached a lightly annotated diagram. Karthik — can you look at the NAT/egress notes and confirm the overlay/underlay behavior (esp BGP vs static) so Stelios has what he needs?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Program Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Private VPC: orthogonal control/data plane ref for review

Thanks — quick technical notes from my side, I annotated the PDF and included a small PNG with callouts (karthik-annotations-20290510.png). Highlights:

- BGP vs static: prefer BGP for dynamic route propagation between Rackline underlay and tenant edge if you're running multiple pods; static is acceptable for single-pod lab deployments but complicates cutovers.
- NAT placement: keep SNAT at the tenant egress edge so we preserve source mapping in our telemetry. Prefer a per-tenant egress IP pool (x.x.x.x/29-style allocation) rather than per-host.
- Return path: ensure symmetric routing to avoid stateful LB asymmetry — we will do health checks on the control plane that assume symmetric 5-tuple reachability.
- mTLS: agree with Marissa — sidecar termination is cleaner. If Rackline terminates at perimeter, you must insert an identity header with the tenant CN and rotate certs via our API.
- Heartbeats & timeouts: please configure a 3s heartbeat interval with a 9s failure window for control-plane RPCs.

I'll also add a short ops table to the Drive doc with firewall ports and expected traffic (control-plane RPC ports, metrics, registry sync).

-- Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
